And that is it. Two home defeats by Leeds in less than 80 hours for Forest. Glasner will have much to ponder with a daunting trip to Anfield coming up on Saturday. All smiles for Farke’s side.

A look at a third for Leeds. Aaronson drives forward before setting Wilson who in turn lays on a first-time pass to Calvert-Lewin. The forward attempts to take his shot first time but can’t get the requisite power on the ball to beat Sels.

A pitch invader makes a brief appearance on the turf but is swiftly ushered away.

According to recent reports, there is a late chance for Forest. Hutchinson’s cross is helped on by Dominguez but that touch inadvertently takes the ball away from Ndoye at the back post.

Forest fans are filing out of the exits and who can blame them?

There will be six minutes of added time.

That just about sums up Forest’s night. Dominguez stands over a free-kick from a dangerous area and, with the box loaded with their most imposing aerial threats, the midfielder sends the ball well over their heads and out for a goal-kick. So poor.

In a recent development, calvert-Lewin is now on for Nmecha. Not really the striker Forest defenders would want to see at this stage of the game.

Another set-piece, this time a Stach corner, is barely dealt with by Forest.

There’s a shout for a handball at the other end as Ndoye spears a cross into the body of Elvedi, but the referee rightly waves the appeals away.

The “oles” ring out from the away end as Leeds string a series of passes together in the corner right in front of it. Forest are looking rather helpless here.

Nottingham Forest 0 Leeds United 2 (Justin) Ampadu releases a throw-in from the right but has to reload as the referee notices some pushing in the box. His next attempt is far too loopy but causes Forest all sorts of trouble, bouncing and bobbling, and coming all the way through a thicket of limbs to Nmecha at the far post. Williams attempts to keep the ball out from a prone position on the goalline under pressure from Justin, who gets the final touch as the ball is bundled over the line.

It's messy but Leeds won't care! 😁Forest fail to deal with the throw-in and Nmecha is there to bundle it in...#EFL | #CarabaoCup pic.twitter.com/oV46fs5RmP.

Jair goes into the book after catching Ampadu in full flight. He never had a prayer of reaching that ball.

The resulting free-kick lands to Amapadu himself in the box, but his effort is deflected behind for a corner which is not up to much.

Goalscorer James is taken off for Bogle, who will offer more mettle down Leeds’ right side as Forest search for an equaliser in the closing stages.

Recent findings suggest that stach has only been on the field for a matter of seconds but comes within a few inches of scoring. Wilson does well on the edge of the box before laying the ball to Stach whose curled effort grazes the outside of the side-netting.

Longstaff’s final contribution to this game is a foul and yellow card as he spreads his legs wide to stop Ndoye breaking away through the middle.

He is replaced by Wilson, as Tanaka and Okafaor also make way, for Stach and Aaronson.

Industry observers note that there’s plenty more endeavour down Forest’s latest-look left side. Hudson Odoi scampers down that flank before cutting inside, and while he’s unable to fashion a chance the intent is correct.

It has been revealed that the substitutions appear to have breathed life into this Forest side. Murillo picks out Dominguez charging forward and Trafford does well to tip the midfielder’s effort behind. The resulting corner comes to nothing.

It has been revealed that glasner resolves he has seen enough and rings the changes. Diomande, Aina, Jesus and Kalimuendo are replaced by Murillo, Netz, Ndoye and Hudson Odoi.

Okafor shows off his dancing feet in the Forest box, pulling off a few stepovers before the ball comes to Ampadu on the edge of the area but his strike is dragged wide.

Chances at both ends! Kalimuendo plays a wonderful ball into the box for Wood to sweep home but Trafford springs into action and makes a stunning save.

Leeds go up the other end, Okafor profiting from a diversionary run from centre-back Elvedi but cannot find the target and double Forest’s lead.

Sources indicate that end-to-end football! ⚡️First Wood, then Okafor - just 19 seconds between the two chances 😮#EFL | #CarabaoCup pic.twitter.com/TGQmtwLNwE.

Leeds are ahead and the inevitable chant from the away supporters is “can we play you every week?”.

This is of course their second meeting in four days and Leeds are on course to record the double.

Forest’s fans are starting to get a little twitchy.

According to recent reports, dan James puts Leeds United in front! ⚽️Tidy finish from the Welshman... #EFL | #CarabaoCup | @LUFC pic.twitter.com/GzWg6zLGLm.

Sources indicate that nottingham Forest 0 Leeds United 1 (James) We finally have a breakthrough. Kalimuendo gives the ball up cheaply in the middle of the park and Longstaff is there to pick up the pieces, darting infield before laying on a perfectly weighted for James to gallop on to, take a touch and sweep beyond Sels. The winger has been Leeds’ biggest threat and deserves that goal.

James finds space down the right - again - and his cross is closed down and deflected behind for a corner.

Longstaff’s floated delivery is tipped away by Sels, but it turns out that the ball went out before coming in so a Forest goal kick is awarded.

A lovely rendition of Mull of Kintyre precedes a short blast of the referee’s whistle and we’re back under way...

Schlager goes into the book instantly for grabbing a handful of Tanaka’s shirt as the Japan international attempted to escape his clutches.

This hasn’t been much of an improvement from Saturday.

It has been revealed that both teams are producing masterclasses in how to misplace passes. Oliver Glasner and Daniel Farke have spent much of the first half looking very frustrated.

James Trafford must be feeling very comfortable and confident of a second successive clean sheet after joining from Manchester City.

Let’s hope for an improvement in the second-half.

Should the scores remain level after 90 minutes, we will go straight to penalties. There’s still a half to play of course, but Forest’s League Cup shoot-out record should be a source of confidence having won seven from eight.

Leeds have only won four from 10.

In a recent development, what a tackle from Joe Rodon! 💥#EFL | #CarabaoCup | @LUFC pic.twitter.com/p5GkzSFEoZ.

It has been revealed that james wins the ball on the halfway line and feeds Okafor down the left. He attempts a deft through-ball into a thicket of bodies but it comes to nothing.

Leeds circulate the ball, working the ball from side to side but there is nowhere near enough movement in front of the ball-player for any meaningful forward passes to be played.

According to recent reports, and, quite aptly, the referee blows up at three seconds past 45 minutes. Certainly not a half for the books.

It has been revealed that another half-chance for Forest! Milenkovic lands on a second ball off a deep free-kick but he cannot keep his strike down. A classic centre-half’s effort if you will.

Ampadu comes over to the left to fire in a long throw-in. Sels comes steaming out of his goal and fumbles the ball but is awarded a free-kick after Muharemovic makes contact. Looked very minimal in all fairness.

In a recent development, oof, a good chance for Aina! Williams’ cross from the left comes all the way through to his opposite wing-back, but Aina’s half-volley sails over. A cracking contact, though.

In a recent development, elvedi and Muharemovic look to be astute buys from Leeds’ perspective. Both assured at the back and the latter especially is confident progressing the ball.

Just as I type that Forest threaten with a ball over the top, but Justin nips in to take the ball away from Wood.

It has been revealed that another decent opening for Leeds after a Forest turnover. Nmecha strides through the middle but Milenkovic is in position to ensure his run comes to nothing.

Sources indicate that what a tackle! Kalimuendo bursts through the middle after Leeds cede possession in a dangerous position. The winger plays in Wood who looks to be through on goal but Rodon comes out of nowhere to telescope a limb and stop the forward in his tracks. Fantastic defensive work from the Welshman.

Nmecha attempts to break beyond the halfway line but is stymied by a swarm of Forest players. He demands a foul from the referee who is not interested in the least.

It’s then Okafor’s turn to put in a dangerous cross from the left, but Nmecha cannot get to it.

Tanaka becomes the first man to go into the book. The ball gets away from him and Jesus puts body between man and ball smartly to win the foul.

Recent findings suggest that tanaka is now dropping into the back line to allow Leeds’ defenders the licence to get wider and higher. Forest will need to be wary of their opponents’ numerical advantage down the flanks.

In a recent development, the game has reached something of a holding pattern as both sides resolve to slow things down, at least temporarily. Forest have settled into a slightly deeper block.

Sensing an opportunity, Ampadu spins in a glorious through-ball between centre-back and full-back for James to gallop on to. He hits the by-line and cuts back to Longstaff, but the midfielder can’t beat Sels. A good chance that probably should have been converted.

Industry observers note that A good chance goes begging! 🫣Longstaff is free for Leeds but fires it straight at Sels...#EFL | #CarabaoCup pic.twitter.com/0UJdfSDQ6w.

Tanaka then turns provider, winning possession in Forest’s half before playing in Longstaff, whose cross-cum-shot does not threaten Sels’ goal.

In a recent development, both sides have physical, quick out-balls, which has made for a frenetic encounter thus far. James rasps in another fierce cross from the right after another sweeping Leeds move, but Nmecha cannot get there and Tanaka fires well over on the follow-up.

Aina’s throw-in, this time from the left, is flicked on to Jesus at the back post and while the forward is able to direct the ball goalwards there is Justin on the line to clear the ball to safety.

Chance! Dominguez slides in Aina down the right channel and the full-back’s mishit cross has Trafford scrambling. He palms the ball behind for a corner, which is headed away for a Forest throw-in on the far side.

Leeds are enjoying a spell of possession here, Tanaka and Longstaff peeling off into the wide areas to collect the ball and disrupt Forest’s mid-block out-of-possession structure. The hosts are more than happy for Leeds to circulate the ball in front of their first line of pressure as, for the second time tonight, Trafford boots it out into touch.

Sources indicate that dominguez stands up a smart cross to the far post where Aina is waiting to head back across goal. Trafford backpedals into Kalimuendo and the referee awards Leeds a free-kick.

Wonderful touch there early in the game from none other than Oliver Glasner.

Forest’s head coach perfectly trapped a high ball as it landed towards him in the technical area.

James shows off his speed for the first time tonight, accelerating down the right before fizzing a dangerous ball into the six-yard box but Forest clear their lines.

Sels goes long to Wood (feels like the right play given his attributes), James lands on the second ball but can only boot the ball into row Z to jeers from the home fans.

According to recent reports, aina launches a long throw-in from the right and it’s headed behind for a corner. Trafford punches the inswinging delivery away and Williams’ effort from the edge of the box sails well over.

Players and mascots walk on to the City Ground turf. A place in the League Cup third round on the line.

Recent findings suggest that reflecting on Saturday’s defeat by Leeds in his programme notes, Glasner wrote: “I saw plenty of encouraging signs from the team on Saturday and I felt we were a lot closer to scoring than we were conceding, especially in the second half. Unfortunately, the small margins were not on our side.

“I thought our defence looked comfortable, but there is still work to be done and the more the players get used to the system we’re operating, the more we’ll see that work come to fruition in competitive matches.

“We have recovered well and will be ready to give our all this evening.”.

Sources indicate that previewing tonight’s League Cup match, Leeds head coach Daniel Farke said: “Our league win is good for our mood and confidence, but this is a ‘do or die’ cup game. Both teams will be motivated to progress, so I expect a tight game. It will be difficult to win on the road again against a tough opponent.”.

When asked what winning a first trophy of his managerial career would mean to him, Farke added: “Well, we weren’t too far away last season. Overall, I would say my form in cup competitions hasn’t been too bad during my career. I’m a substantial believer in these competitions, I like the ‘do or die’ mentality. I would never say no to another good cup run.”.

The hosts’ kits tonight will include Carabao Cup sleeve patches with the number four on them, in recognition of the club’s League Cup triumphs in 1978, 1979, 1989 and 1990.

This is Forest and Leeds Part 2, just four days after they clashed in the Premier League.

Daniel Farke ruined the Oliver Glasner welcoming party on Saturday with a 1-0 smash-and-grab victory at the death.

Both managers have gone relatively strong for this tie, with only a sprinkling of debuts.

Ousmane Diomande, the £34m signing from Sporting, makes his first appearance while there is a first start for Xaver Schlager.

The major breaking news is that Forest are smashing their club record to sign Chelsea forward Liam Delap for £45m.

Delap will undergo a medical at Forest on Wednesday with the deal potentially rising to £50m after add-ons.

It eclipses the previous transfer record of £37.5m for winger Omari Hutchinson.

Oliver Glasner has prioritised the addition of a latest centre-forward this summer and Delap ticks pretty much every box for him.

In a recent development, welcome to live coverage of the Carabao Cup second-round match between Nottingham Forest and Leeds United. This will be the sides’ second meeting at the City Ground in four days after Anton Stach’s late free-kick decided an attritional contest on the Premier League’s opening weekend. Forest’s latest head coach Oliver Glasner is something of a cup specialist, though, with FA Cup, Europa League and Conference League titles to his name and he will relish the opportunity to right the wrongs of Saturday in front of the Forest faithful.

The Austrian is Forest’s fifth head coach in less than 12 months and he will look to arrest the churn by bringing to the City Ground the success he enjoyed with Crystal Palace. During pre-season, the Austrian moulded Forest into his preferred 3-4-3 shape, placing summer acquisition Ousmane Diomande alongside the existing central-defensive partnership of Murillo and Nikola Milenković. Here, Diomande gets his Forest debut and Glasner brings in talisman Chris Wood from the start.

Daniel Farke will have been delighted to see his Leeds side continue their excellent form in pre-season – which included victories over Liverpool, Red Bull Leipzig and Augsburg – into the season proper. Although Leeds arrive at the City Ground shorn of attacking options Wilfried Gnonto, Noah Okafor and Mateo Joseph through injury, Farke still shuffles the pack in the forward positions with this weekend’s visit of Brentford to Elland Road in mind.

Feyenoord preserved their four-point advantage over champions PSV after coming away with a point from Eindhoven thanks to an improved second-half performance.

PSV dominated the first half as they deployed a close-passing, tiki-taka style to stifle Feyenoord, but only had Guus Til’s well-taken volley after 20 minutes to show for it.

Ten minutes after the break Feyenoord equalised when Anis Hadj Moussa was given too much space to charge down the right flank and bend a shot inside the far post.

The Algerian had a good chance for a second towards the end, while PSV goalkeeper Matej Kovar had to be alert to keep out a header by Nacho Ferri from close range.

Industry observers note that “We were by far the better team today and had the better chances,” noted PSV coach Peter Bosz. “We started the second half badly and made a mistake, after which Hadj Moussa scored. And even then we could have won it.”.

Ajax overtook PSV to close the gap at the top to three points with a hard-fought win at Sparta. Veteran striker Jens Toornstra scored for Sparta on his 500th Eredivisie appearance, but Abdellah Ouazane and Tolu Arokodare, the scorers against Atalanta in midweek, were on target again to claim the win for Ajax.

Twente moved up to fourth place as two late goals by Sondre Ørjasæter and Lucas Vennegoor of Hesselink earned a 2-0 win at AZ Alkmaar, who like Twente and PSV have 20 points.

Fortuna Sittard also snatched the points late on against Excelsior as Rodrigo Guth headed in a corner in injury time to keep the Limburg club in sixth place, two points further back.

At the other end of the table, the return of Adrie Koster as veteran coach brought no relief to Willem II, who crashed to a 6-1 home defeat to Cambuur.

The Tilburgers remain four points behind ADO Den Haag, who were unable to keep up the momentum of last week’s win against PSV as they lost 3-2 at home to Heerenveen.

Telstar lost by the same margin at Go Ahead Eagles, whose striker Søren Tengstedt netted twice in the first half to lead the Eredivisie scoring charts with eight goals.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It looked like this was going to be a night for “one of their own”, but Tottenham Hotspur’s latest significant-money arrival, Sávio, stole the headlines to crank up the excitement at his fresh club.

Mikey Moore had set Spurs on their way to what proved a comfortable Carabao Cup success over Championship club Charlton Athletic and heard his name sung by the home fans.

But Sávio stepped off the substitutes’ bench to take the limelight with a late goal just a few days after completing his expensive switch from Manchester City, and head coach Roberto De Zerbi is demanding many more to come.

“A perfect day for him,” remarked De Zerbi. “His biggest improvement is to increase the number of goals. He is one of the best wingers, but the best wingers score many goals and I spoke with him two days ago, and we put the goal at 10-12 goals.

According to recent reports, “We need 10-12 goals from the wingers. Last season, we suffered too much because the number of goals were not enough.”.

"What an introduction!"Sávio scores a brilliant goal on his Spurs debut! 👏 pic.twitter.com/WgmcfgeNpX.

Having watched some of Tottenham’s signings fall to a 3-0 Premier League defeat by Brentford a few days earlier, Sávio’s late impact was the perfect lift for the Spurs supporters.

The club have committed to spending almost £400m this summer, leading to debate by outsiders over whether it will prove to be money well spent and huge waves of excitement within the fanbase.

A deal that could be worth as much as £85m, if add-ons are achieved, for Sávio certainly raised some eyebrows, but the Brazilian provided the perfect response by scoring just 11 minutes into his debut as a late substitute.

In the 82nd minute, Sávio cut in from the flank and scored with a shot past Charlton goalkeeper Tiernan Brooks. He and the Spurs crowd thought he had a second a few minutes later, but his shot hit Ben Davies on its way into the net and the defender was credited with the goal.

Having sung for Moore earlier in the game, the Spurs fans wasted no time in trying out their newly introduced song for Sávio, inspired by the Spandau Ballet hit Gold.

Moore has been expected to move to Cologne on loan, but provided a reminder of his talent by opening the scoring in the first half with only his second goal for the club.

It has been revealed that what a hit from Mikey Moore! ⚪ pic.twitter.com/OgSM4qhiqs.

“We have to understand the best solution,” De Zerbi noted. “I would like to keep him. He’s young but a good player, but we can’t make the wrong decision. He needs to play, he needs to get games inside him.”.

Cutting in from the right, where Sávio is primed to play, Moore surged past his marker and shot from just inside the box. Brooks should have stopped it, but the ball flew past him and into the net.

Three minutes after Moore’s opener, Dominic Solanke scored his first goal since March to offer a reminder of what he can still give De Zerbi, who is poised to welcome Omar Marmoush to Tottenham.

In a recent development, buoyed by his first-half goal, Moore skipped his way around a couple of tackles at the start of the second period but his low cross was cut out. The Spurs fans responded by singing “he’s one of our own.”.

Substitute Kevin Danso netted with his first touch from a header, before Sávio was introduced to steal the show, despite a late consolation goal from Charlton’s Lloyd Jones.

Recent findings suggest that kevin Danso scores with his first touch since coming on! ⚪ pic.twitter.com/oqUU7wjoJW.

The victory set up a tough third-round trip to Anfield to face Liverpool for Tottenham, but De Zerbi said: “It’s a great game. If we want to win the competition we have to win the games.

Sources indicate that “Sometimes in this competition, it can happen that you play against massive teams. It’s a great challenge for the players, for me, for our clubs. We have to arrive ready to play in our style, with personality, ready to play a game following the work we are doing on the training ground.”.

Tottenham had looked rather lethargic but they take the lead in emphatic style. The 19-year-old cuts inside from the right and comes across the face of the Charlton penalty area. Recent findings suggest that the first booking of the night goes the way of the hosts as Bergvall cynically takes down Apter as the Charlton man drove towards the Tottenham penalty area. You feel like Charlton need to take advantage of opportunities like this if they want to win this tie. The ball is clipped in and it comes off Van Hecke’s head for a corner. Tottenham clear their lines initially but Charlton keep it alive. Docherty strikes it first time from the edge of the Tottenham box and forces Kinsky into a good save diving to his left.

It has been revealed that that probably sums up Tottenham’s night thus far. Davies pings a lovely diagonal ball out to Moore in space down Tottenham’s right. Moore waits for the overlapping run of Gray before playing the pass but Gray’s attempted cross from the right side of the box is terrible and goes behind for a goal kick. Roberto De Zerbi is promptly out of his seat!

In a recent development, roberto De Zerbi was keen to see his side show a reaction to their defeat at Brentford on Saturday. Unsurprisingly, they are dominating possession but have not posed much of a threat going forward.

There has been a goal at St James’ Park and it is the visitors West Brom who have taken the lead over Newcastle. Price has scored directly from a free-kick and the Championship side lead.

Sources indicate that things have just gone from bad to worse for Charlton. Whilst one of their centre-backs is being stretchered off in Sichenje, their other centre-half Koumetio, who used to be on the books at Liverpool, is also down. Koumetio, like Sichenje, is going to come off. McNamara and Jones, who like Koumetio used to be at Liverpool, are coming on. Charlton have had to change both centre-backs inside the opening quarter of an hour.

Industry observers note that sichenje did try to continue but he has gone back down again and his night appears to be over. The question will be has he done more damage to his knee trying to play on? The stretcher is being brought on and it will be a sorry end to his night.

Moore wins Tottenham a corner out on the right, which summer signing Fernandes will take. His delivery is headed away and the danger is gone.

According to recent reports, sichenje has now got back to his feet so he may have avoided a serious injury but we will see if he can continue. It looks like he will try to continue at least.

Play is halted as Charlton defender Sichenje looks to be in a lot of pain as he bangs the ground in frustration. It appears to be his left knee and the visitors may be forced into an early change.

Inside the opening minute, Solanke thinks he will have a chance on goal as the ball is played in behind but there is too much on it and the ball goes through to Brooks in the Charlton goal.

We are under way in north London.

It has been revealed that both sides emerge from the tunnel at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium and we are just moments away from kick-off north London. Here is a reminder of how the two sides line up this evening:.

“Tottenham are a top club. Top manager and players so it is a wonderful opportunity to test ourselves. We are a way off these yet, but that is eventually the goal.”.

Recent findings suggest that after nine years at Anfield, Andy Robertson has swapped Liverpool for Tottenham this summer. He started for Tottenham against Brentford and is on the bench tonight ahead of what could be his first home game for the club.

Omar Marmoush will undergo a medical at Tottenham Hotspur on Wednesday on loan with an obligation to pay Manchester City £60m for the Egypt forward next summer.

Marmoush will become the second signing from City this week after Savinho – who has asked to be referred to as Sávio – completed his move.

City signed Marmoush two seasons ago from Eintracht Frankfurt for £59m and the German club do not have a sell-on clause, meaning they will not receive a fee from the deal.

A place in the League Cup third round is at stake as Tottenham host Charlton in a London derby at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium. The last competitive meeting between these sides came in the FA Cup back in January 2011, with Tottenham winning that game 3-0 at White Hart Lane. A then 19-year-old Andros Townsend made his debut that day and scored, with Jermain Defoe scoring a brace.

Tottenham’s Premier League campaign got off to the worst possible start as they lost 3-0 at Brentford last weekend. Tottenham have been very busy during this summer transfer window and that has continued this week. Savio (formerly Savinho) has arrived from Manchester City in a deal that could be worth £85m and the Brazilian could make his Tottenham debut tonight, having been registered in time.

It has been revealed that “I think in attacking positions we need players capable one-on one, to create something, to create a chance to score,” Roberto De Zerbi remarked. “In terms of one-on-one, he [Savio] is one of the best players, especially since 2024. He can play on the right side, on the left side. I have known him from a long time, I spoke with him when he went to Manchester City. He is a big player for us.

“I do not know if I am the right man [to get the most out of Savio], but for sure he has to achieve. I think a player who is so good in one-on-one, so good at creating chances to score, to be complete, he has to score. If you analyse the other best wingers in the world, many of them, they score 10 to 15 goals per season. He has the qualities. Maybe his habits, he has to change habits, because he has to be focused on the assists, the one-on-one dribbling and also to score.”.

Sources indicate that omar Marmoush is closing in on an initial loan deal from Manchester City but that move is not complete and thus he is not available for Tottenham tonight. Micky van der Ven and Pedro Porro are both available having missed Tottenham’s loss at Brentford but the hosts are still without Xavi Simons, Pape Sarr, Dejan Kulusevski and Wilson Odobert.

In a recent development, charlton have made the perfect start to their Championship campaign; a 2-1 home win over Derby was followed up by a 2-1 victory at recently-relegated West Ham. Nathan Jones’ side earned their place in the League Cup second round with a 3-1 win at Cheltenham in the first round.

It has been revealed that “We have to be very organised and very professional, they [Tottenham] are a top team,” Jones remarked. “They have a great manager and a brilliant group of players. They already had a Premier League squad and they have spent, what is reaching about, I do not know, £300 million or something like that. It is a wonderful test, we have to be right near our best and do both sides of the game very well. Of course, you want to test yourself against the best managers and you want to test yourself against the best teams. For us, this is not our priority, the Championship is our priority, but this is the next game and therefore it is the most key.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results.

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results.

Acceptance of homosexuality in Dutch sports clubs has declined significantly in the last generation, according to a survey of attitudes by the Mulier Institute.

The organisation found that 66% of people had no objection to a fellow member of a sports club being gay, while in 2008 the figure was 85%.

Just over half (55%) of respondents said they had no problem sharing a shower with a gay team-mate of the same sex, which also represented a drop from 73% in 2008.

The Mulier Institute said the findings reflected a social trend that has also been seen in schools, where the proportion of boys aged between 12 and 16 with a positive view of homosexuality has dropped from 40% to 22% since 2021.

The Dutch Olympic Committee NOC*NSF mentioned the findings were “highly regrettable” and pledged to step up its efforts to make sport more inclusive.

But the John Blankenstein Foundation, which campaigns for LGBT emancipation in sport, said it had noticed declining enthusiasm for its workshops and growing numbers of parents who voiced objections.

Karin Blankenstein, who set up the organisation in 2008, told NOS: “I get the sensitivity around transgender people in sport at the top level, but this is about amateur sport.”.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM.

Il Belgio è una grande squadra. Le grandi squadre nascono da un grande centrocampo e il Belgio lo ha. In Nazionale si vede il vero De Bruyne, noi abbiamo contrapposto calciatori che non possono certo essere considerati di pari livello. L'Italia è una squadra che esprime i valori del calcio italiano, guardate anche sul piano fisico: il Belgio ci ha sovrastato. È un bravo allenatore. Ma il materiale a disposizione è questo. E quando incontriamo le squadre che giocano il calcio attuale si vedono i valori. Mi spaventa vedere quale sarà il programma del nuovo presidente federale. Con Malagò, tutta la vita. All'inizio non ero favorevole a lui, considerato anche che sono suo amico. Pensavo non avesse il coraggio di fare certe cose, invece ce l'ha. Dopo il caos ha scelto lui Mancini e non s'è fatto imporre altri nomi. E ha preso l'allenatore migliore, quello più giusto.

Recent findings suggest that la Lazio è la sorpresa e sta offrendo prestazioni importanti, ma deve ancora affrontare le squadre più forti. Tranne la Juve che per me è l'altra grande delusione di questo campionato.

A late equaliser for Fortuna Sittard in De Kuip proved costly for Feyenoord as PSV and Twente racked up huge victories to move within two points of the Eredivisie leaders.

Feyenoord paid the price for failing to finish off the Limburgers, with Luciano Valente’s 59th-minute goal the only reward for their dominance.

Fortuna equalised with four minutes left when Shiloh ’t Zand, on loan from Feyenoord, was allowed to run through to the penalty area and beat Tjark Ernst with a low shot.

Sources indicate that feyenoord coach Giovanni van Bronckhorst made no effort to hide his disappointment. “We know that Fortuna are the kind of team who can score from the few attacks they have,” he mentioned. “If you don’t score the goals, things like this can happen.”.

Second-placed Ajax are a point behind after a narrow win at home against AZ ended an 11-match winless streak against the Alkmaar club, as Tolu Arokodare’s early header proved decisive.

Twente recorded the biggest win of the weekend with a 9-0 demolition of Excelsior in Rotterdam, with Wout Weghorst scoring four times and Sondre Ørjasaeter notching up five assists.

Excelsior collapsed following the fifth-minute dismissal of Nesto Groen for a reckless high challenge. The home side were 5-0 down at half-time, with Weghorst claiming a hat-trick in the opening 33 minutes.

PSV bagged seven goals in a one-sided encounter with bottom club Willem II, with all the goals coming from different scorers including Ricardo Pepi, who came on in the second half after a six-week absence through injury.

Telstar opened up a three-point gap at the bottom over ADO Den Haag with a 4-2 win against Utrecht in a painful return to Velsen-Zuid for Telstar’s former coach Anthony Correia.

ADO went down 1-0 in Zwolle, with PEC’s Dylan Mbayo scoring the only goal with a first-time finish on the stroke of half-time.

The match between Cambuur Leeuwarden and Go Ahead Eagles was suspended in the 82nd minute after visiting fans threw fireworks onto the pitch.

The clubs agreed with the KNVB not to play the final minutes and allow Cambuur’s 4-0 advantage to stand as the final result.

Go Ahead’s director Jan-Willem van Dop said the club would take action against those responsible: “I am ashamed on behalf a small group of supporters who ruined things for the club and a large hare of the fans in the away end,” he said.

Cambuur Leeuwarden 4-0 Go Ahead Eagles.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Mourinho, the former Chelsea, Manchester United and Tottenham Hotspur manager, will return to London to resume hostilities against last season’s beaten finalists.
  • Other reunions from Thursday’s draw include Manchester City travelling to Barcelona, to whom they last week sold Rodri, and Liverpool visiting Inter Milan, who have signed Curtis Jones.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Arsenal will host old nemesis José Mourinho’s Real Madrid in the league phase of the Champions League.

Mourinho, the former Chelsea, Manchester United and Tottenham Hotspur manager, will return to London to resume hostilities against last season’s beaten finalists.

Other reunions from Thursday’s draw include Manchester City travelling to Barcelona, to whom they last week sold Rodri, and Liverpool visiting Inter Milan, who have signed Curtis Jones.

It has been revealed that arsenal will also travel to Harry Kane’s Bayern Munich, while United will host the Germans as well on their Champions League return in a repeat of the legendary 1999 final. Michael Carrick’s side will also visit Cesc Fàbregas’s Como.

Mourinho last managed at the Emirates Stadium in March 2021, barely a month before his sacking by Spurs.

During his two spells as Chelsea manager, Mourinho famously had run-ins with Arsenal’s Arsène Wenger.

Mourinho called Wenger a “specialist in failure” after the Frenchman failed to add to his three Premier League titles following his Portuguese counterpart’s arrival in London in 2004.

Last season, Mikel Arteta finally ended Arsenal’s long wait to be crowned champions of England but agonisingly missed out on European glory.

Sources indicate that verdict Premier League champions should not be daunted by any game, but Real Madrid – with Mourinho in control – has the feel of a defining match of the group stage. Facing Kane in Munich does not seem any easier. Some tough assignments here including a trip to Napoli but the pot-four teams seem straightforward for Mikel Arteta.

Verdict Playing against the European champions and travelling to Barcelona will be a true test of how much progress Enzo Maresca has made in the short time he has been at the Etihad Stadium. City’s other games do not look easy either but they should be defeating teams such as Sporting Lisbon and Porto – at least they would be expected to under Pep Guardiola.

Verdict The San Siro was where Arne Slot began to turn results around last season and Iraola getting a win there would be a big statement. Atlético staged a comeback at Anfield in 2020 and the repeat fixture will be tight. But there are enough winnable games there for Liverpool to reach the next round.

Verdict They will face a wall of noise in Istanbul when they play Galatasaray, but Villa will look to get points from the game. There are some tasty destinations for travelling fans and getting results there will ease the pressure on the match against PSG, who have been rattled by Villa before but remain a difficult opponent. The Nou Camp is a place where momentum can change in a season – for good or bad.

Verdict The repeat of the 1999 final is the standout fixture, but Michael Carrick should be looking beyond that match for the points needed to progress. He has been given a tough set of away games to navigate. They are winnable but difficult. So those games at Old Trafford will be very key.

That brings our coverage of the Champions League draw to an end, as the 36 teams found which eight teams they will be facing in the league phase of this season’s tournament. Thanks for joining us!

The league phase will kick off on 8 September and will be wrapped up after all teams play at the same time on 27 January.

The top eight teams of the league phase progress to the last 16 automatically, while teams that finish between ninth and 24th will be forced to navigate a play-off tie to reach the knockout stages.

So we have 144 fixtures decided but there are certainly a few heavyweight contests which stand out:.

Recent findings suggest that that is pots two and three done. Just the pot four teams to sort out now, finding out which other pot four teams they will face.

Recent findings suggest that some crackers in there. Up next we will be finding out all the opponents for the pot two teams.

They will face two teams from each pot, with one home game and one away game per pot, while they cannot play a team from their country.

This will be done for all nine teams from pot one, before the same process takes place for pot two teams, though they will already know their pot one opponents. Pot three teams will then find out their pot three and four opponents, before the pot four sides are allocated their fixtures against each other.

This season is the third under the newly introduced format, with a league phase instead of a group stage, and Uefa has confirmed that fixtures that have taken place in the league phase of the two previous seasons cannot be repeated this time around.

For example, Liverpool cannot host Real Madrid in the league phase this term after welcoming the 15-time European champions to Anfield at this stage of the previous two campaigns. Andoni Iraola’s side could, however, travel to the Bernabeu for an away meeting with Madrid.

Similarly, Arsenal will not be travelling to San Siro to face Inter, but could host the Serie A champions at the Emirates.

Arsenal finished top of the league phase last season after winning all eight fixtures and it resulted in a favourable run to the final, facing Bayer Leverkusen, Sporting and Atletico Madrid.

Liverpool, meanwhile, topped the league phase in the 2024-25 campaign – the first season with the new format – but fell at the first hurdle in the knockout stages after being drawn against Paris St-Germain.

The Ligue 1 side have proven that it’s not essential to be firing the whole way through the tournament, finishing 15th and 11th in the league phase in the last two seasons but going on to lift the trophy on both occasions.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Après le carton de son livre Foot Sentimental paru il y a 3 ans aux éditions Le Cherche midi, Dominique Rocheteau a fait paraître le mois dernier dans la même maison Soif d'Idéal. L'Ange Vert revient dans ce bouquin - anecdotes à l'appui - sur la Rocheteaumania qui a envahi la France après le mythique quart de finale retour de Coupe d'Europe des Clubs Champions qui s'est déroulé le 17 mars 1976 dans le Chaudron. Extraits.

"C'est seulement le lendemain de notre victoire contre Kiev, puis dans les jours qui ont suivi, que j'ai commencé à prendre la mesure de ce qui venait de se passer. Peu à peu, j'ai perçu l'ampleur de cette vague verte qui n'allait cesser de grandir, et de ce que ce match allait changer dans ma vie. À l'entraînement, une foule que je n'avais encore jamais vue pour un simple décrassage nous attendait : à l'entrée, à la sortie, tout autour du terrain. Que du vert. Cette fois, j'ai pu saluer mes parents à la sortie du stade, juste avant qu'ils ne reprennent la route. J’étais heureux, bien sûr, mais je l'avoue un peu perdu, déconcerté, face à cet engouement auquel je n'étais absolument pas préparé.

According to recent reports, J'ai vraiment pris conscience que quelque chose avait changé lors de nos déplacements en championnat après Kiev. C'était comme si toute la France était derrière nous. Et puis, il y avait les médias, plus seulement sportifs : Paris Match, Télé 7 Jours, Rock & Folk, Rolling Stones, Salut les copains, Pif Gadget… Je ne lisais pas les journaux, je ne regardais pas la télévision. J'étais un peu dans mon monde, mais désormais je devais « apprendre » à me raconter. J'acceptais les demandes, plus par politesse que par réelle envie. Je me retrouvais souvent pris de court, parfois même paniqué. Je n'avais pas d'agent. Les journalistes passaient par le club pour leurs demandes d'interview, et je me sentais obligé d'accepter. À 20 ans, je ne contrôlais rien. Un jour, je me suis rendu compte que j'avais donné une interview pour un magazine érotique… quand ils m'ont envoyé le numéro. C'est aussi après Kiev que l'on a commencé à m'appeler l’« Ange vert », un surnom que j'ai mis du temps à apprécier.

Recent findings suggest that ce qui m'a le plus désarçonné, ce sont ces sacs de courriers qui ont commencé à arriver. Que faire de tout ça ? Je lisais quelques lettres, mais il y en avait des milliers. Il y avait de tout : des demandes en mariage, des déclarations d'amour, des confidences, des photos, des messages, comme si nous nous connaissions depuis toujours. Après les vacances d'été et celles de Noël, quand je revenais de Charente-Maritime, le secrétaire de l'AS Saint-Étienne m'invitait à passer récupérer au stade des sacs postaux. « Il y en a plusieurs kilos ». Je devinais à son ton que cela représentait une charge de travail. Ils étaient remplis de lettres et parfois de cassettes audio de filles envoyant des compliments ou des messages, par exemple : « Dominique, j'aimerais bien que l'on se voit ». Certaines glissaient même un chewing-gum à l'intérieur. Beaucoup de lettres venaient de filles. Certaines m'avouaient qu'elles m'aimaient.

Recent findings suggest that il y avait aussi des plaisanteries comme cette lettre émanant de lycéennes d'un établissement religieux en région parisienne qui suggérait mon mariage avec une fille « de bonne famille » de leur entourage. D'autres donnaient des recettes miracles pour faire cesser les rhumes ou bien améliorer le tonus. Des collégiens racontaient aussi le plaisir qu'ils avaient à chanter pendant leurs cours la chanson « Allez les Verts » pour embêter leurs professeurs. Beaucoup de lettres venaient d'Afrique, où Saint-Étienne était très aimé. Certaines étaient longues, parfois plusieurs pages et vraiment très belles. Mais aussi des pays de l'Est -Pologne, Allemagne de l'Est, Tchécoslovaquie - d'où de nombreux collectionneurs m'envoyaient des photos parues dans les magazines afin que je les signe. J'en reçois encore aujourd'hui au siège du club qui me les fait suivre à chaque fois.

Mes amis Hugues et Louis - qui habitait à Saint-Héand et préparait son concours du barreau - et moi, nous nous asseyions par terre dans la salle à manger pour trier le courrier. Impossible de répondre à tout le monde. Nous envoyions une photo dédicacée à ceux qui avaient joint une enveloppe timbrée à leur nom. Certains glissaient même un billet de 20 ou 50 francs pour recevoir une photo signée. Nous remettions ensuite les enveloppes à la postière de Saint-Héand qui nous félicitait : « Joli travail ! », avant de les oblitérer. À travers toutes ces petites histoires, j'étais à la fois touché mais aussi terriblement gêné. Tout cela me paraissait énorme, démesuré. Dans la rue, j'appréciais les marques de sympathie même si elles me mettaient mal à l'aise. Je ne savais pas toujours quoi dire, alors je répondais par un sourire.

Un matin de juillet 1976, j'étais en vacances chez mes parents. Je dormais encore tandis que ma mère et Louis prenaient le café dans le jardin. Un jeune homme s'est présenté derrière le grillage et a demandé à me voir. Ma mère lui a demandé s'il me connaissait. Devant sa réponse affirmative et son insistance, elle a fini par le laisser entrer. Ils sont venus me réveiller. « Il y a un ami qui veut te voir ». Je me suis levé, surpris. « Je ne vous connais pas » -  « Si, je vous ai vu à un match »… « Qu'est-ce que vous voulez ? » « Un autographe ». Je me suis exécuté et il est reparti ravi. Je suis resté partagé entre la satisfaction de faire plaisir et le malaise de voir ma vie privée ainsi envahie.

It has been revealed that une autre fois, peu après avoir fait construire mon chalet à La Gimont, je suis rentré de l'entraînement et j'ai constaté que mon chat, Diamant, avait disparu. Une femme était venue chez moi, l'avait emmenée et avait fait savoir à mon entourage que si je voulais le récupérer, je devais me rendre personnellement chez elle à Veauche, à une dizaine de kilomètres. Mon ami Louis a tenté de la raisonner, en vain. Que faire ? Il n'était pas question pour moi de céder à ce chantage. Je ne voulais pas y aller, mais je tenais à récupérer mon chat. Yves, le frère de Louis, a alors appelé la gendarmerie de Saint-Galmier. Les gendarmes se sont rendus à Veauche et ont réussi à convaincre la dame de rendre Diamant. Ils n'ont toutefois pas pu le ramener eux-mêmes. Sur leur conseil, Louis a sauté dans sa voiture pour aller le chercher. Quand il est arrivé, le chat était couché sur un coussin, sur une chaise. La femme lui a lancé : « Voyez, il avait déjà pris ses marques. » Grâce à Louis et à l'intervention des gendarmes, j'ai pu récupérer Diamant et une fois de plus mesurer la chance que j'avais d'avoir des amis en or. 1976 a été une année folle. Depuis Kiev, tout avait changé autour de moi, mais je n'ai jamais vraiment cherché à me protéger ni à mettre de la distance entre moi et les autres. Je voulais simplement vivre une vie normale, comme les autres jeunes de mon époque.".

Dual passports issue continues to plague Dutch-based footballers

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results.

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results.

Dutch-born footballers who were called up to play for former colonies such as Suriname and Indonesia are still in limbo over their national status, six months after the “passportgate” crisis first flared up.

Suriname’s parliament passed a law in September enabling players who are selected for the national team to gain citizenship automatically.

But the Dutch immigration service IND said the law passed in Suriname made no difference to the rules on dual nationality in the Netherlands.

“The fact that Surinamese nationality has been obtained by legal means is not enough on its own to qualify for one of the exceptional categories under our law,” a spokesman for the Dutch justice ministry told broadcaster NOS.

The law was intended to settle the question of dual nationality for footballers, which arose last March when NAC Breda challenged the eligibility of Go Ahead Eagles defender Dean James.

James took Indonesian citizenship last year after accepting an invitation to play for the national team, but under Dutch dual nationality rules he was required to give up his original passport.

Industry observers note that the Dutch football association KNVB rolled out an investigation into the employment status of players who were called up by countries such as Suriname, Cape Verde and Indonesia. In the meantime it arranged for Dutch-based players to be given temporary work permits so they could keep playing for their clubs.

Losing Dutch nationality also stripped them of their EU citizenship, meaning they would need to obtain visas and meet stricter criteria, such as an annual salary threshold of €600,000, to be eligible to play in the Eredivisie.

Several players have passed up invitations to join the Surinamese squad because of the uncertainty, including Danilho Doekhi of Lazio, Milan van Ewijk of Coventry City and Jayden Oosterwolde of Fenerbahçe.

National team manager Henk Fraser noted it was “inexplicable” that players’ livelihoods were being damaged by their desire to play international football.

According to recent reports, “Both countries have to get together and clarify the situation,” he told NOS. “This is a straightforward case of people following their hearts and wanting to play for Suriname, but not knowing where they stand.”.

Some players said they felt misled by the Surinamese football association, which told them they were playing for the national team on “sports passports” that allowed them to remain Dutch citizens.

Former Feyenoord winger Jean-Paul Boëtius stated he only discovered after he was first called up for Suriname last year that he had inadvertently renounced his Dutch citizenship as a result.

Shortly afterwards he received a letter from the city council in Rotterdam telling him to hand in his Dutch passport, which he had recently renewed, because it was no longer valid.

It has been revealed that “I now have a sticker in my Surinamese passport that indicates I have a residency permit allowing me to live in the Netherlands,” he told NOS. “But that’s only for a year. It’s a very difficult situation. I want to become Dutch again. I was born and brought up here.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

La retraite internationale de Romelu Lukaku (33 ans), meilleur buteur de l'histoire en sélection belge (94 pions en 135 sélections), laisse un grand vide chez les Diables Rouges. Comme l'a souligné hier La Dernière Heure Les Sports +, les candidats ne manquent pas mais le Diablotin Lucas Stassin part de loin. Extraits.

"Charles De Ketelaere a pris le relais, dans un autre style mais sans être remis en question. Il est le titulaire incontesté en pointe, même s'il joue à une autre position à l'Atalanta. Il sera d'ailleurs intéressant de voir s'il osera prendre le n°9 au prochain rassemblement. Qui pour doubler CDK dorénavant ? Le casting est large et étonnamment ouvert.

It has been revealed that loïs Openda peut y penser, lui qui retrouvait peu à peu ses sensations à Lyon avant de se blesser et de manquer ce rassemblement. Mais parviendra-t-il enfin à éclore en équipe nationale alors qu'il fêtera bientôt son 27e anniversaire ? Il n'a inscrit que trois buts chez les Diables jusqu'à présent.

Industry observers note that hugo Cuypers, le Belge le plus prolifique ces derniers mois, peut espérer monter en grade après avoir fêté sa première sélection. Mais lui aura 30 ans au prochain rassemblement. Il ne sera pas une solution à long terme et devra aussi prouver qu'il peut avoir le niveau en évoluant dans le championnat mexicain.

It has been revealed that L'avant-centre le plus prometteur en Belgique, c'est probablement Matias Fernandez-Pardo (21 ans), mais avec un tout autre profil que Lukaku et De Ketelaere. Acheté 60 M€ par Newcastle cet été, il possède une vitesse et une puissance de jambes assez phénoménales. Le tout avec un vrai sens du but.

Le sélectionneur a aussi une autre option, très différente : le faux 9. Deux joueurs sont capables de prendre ce rôle, que CDK peut parfois avoir selon le moment du match. On pense à Leandro Trossard, qui avait par moments dépanné Arsenal devant, et à Mika Godts, barré sur les flancs par Jeremy Doku et Diego Moreira. Lui aussi a déjà évolué en faux 9, à l'Ajax.

L'idée sera aussi de regarder dans le réservoir belge. En Espoirs, trois attaquants prouvent qu'ils ont des qualités : Lucas Stassin, Romeo Vermant et Norman Bassette. À tel point que le coach Gill Swerts a cherché un système pour en utiliser au moins deux des trois en même temps. Leur évolution en club fera beaucoup de leur avenir à court terme chez les Diables.".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Lotito e Fabiani hanno garantito a Gattuso che i giocatori più importanti non partiranno nella sessione invernale.

It has been revealed that la Juventus prepara un'offerta da 40 milioni di euro per Kenneth Taylor a gennaio, ma la Lazio non vuole cederlo durante l'inverno. i bianconeri seguono il centrocampista olandese dall'estate e puntano ad anticipare la concorrenza inglese. Lotito e Fabiani hanno garantito a Gattuso che non partiranno giocatori importanti, soprattutto se il mercato in entrata resterà bloccato.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM.

Recent findings suggest that la Lazio ha acquistato Taylor meno di dieci mesi fa per meno di 17 milioni di euro. Una cessione a 40 milioni produrrebbe una plusvalenza, anche tenendo conto del 10% che spetta ancora all'Ajax.

La linea del club sulle cessioni invernali è riassunta nella risposta «se ne parla a giugno», ribadita agli agenti che stanno presentando offerte per altri giocatori. Tra queste c'è una proposta del Brentford da 25 milioni per Isaksen. Per Taylor, Brighton e Bournemouth guardano a giugno, mentre la Juve vorrebbe muoversi già a gennaio.

It has been revealed that conta anche la volontà del calciatore. Taylor guadagna 1,7 milioni di euro e la Juventus gli offrirebbe il doppio. Il suo accordo prevede inoltre un premio fedeltà di 190mila euro per ogni sessione di mercato trascorsa alla Lazio: il primo assegno è arrivato a settembre, il secondo potrebbe arrivare a febbraio.

Il premio e l'attuale primo posto della Lazio sono incentivi a restare, ma Taylor, a 24 anni, ha grandi ambizioni e ha risentito dell'ultima esclusione dalla nazionale olandese. Il ct Xavi ha richiamato la concorrenza e i ritorni di Kluivert e De Jong, lasciando aperta la porta. Il colpo rimediato al Maradona non dovrebbe impedirgli di giocare sabato contro il Lecce, alla ripresa del campionato.

A Roma il centrocampista è cresciuto. Contro Cagliari e Napoli ha recuperato palloni, accompagnato le ripartenze e partecipato alla costruzione del gioco. Ha segnato il gol decisivo a Parma e, contro il Sassuolo, ha realizzato una rete e fornito un assist. Sa inserirsi, rifinire e contrastare; con Belahyane e Frattesi ha contribuito al funzionamento del centrocampo.

Pochi mesi fa sulla sua permanenza pesavano i primi sei mesi a Roma, l'addio di giocatori importanti, il mercato a saldo zero, le ambizioni ridimensionate e motivi personali e sentimentali. Poi sono arrivati le vittorie e la fiducia, e Taylor è diventato un leader della Lazio.

Gattuso ha espresso così la volontà di non perdere i suoi giocatori a gennaio: «Spero che a gennaio nessuno venga nel mio ufficio. Potrei chiudere la porta a chiave».

According to recent reports, S'il n'a pas encore joué de match officiel en équipe première sous le maillot vert depuis son arrivée dans le Forez le 2 février dernier, Marten-Chris Paalberg, actuellement sous contrat avec l'ASSE jusqu'en 2030, a démarré cet automne 3 matches avec la réserve : 1 en Challenge Espoirs (0-2 face au Mans) et 2 en National 2 (1-1 à Montpellier). Venant d'enchaîner 2 succès en équipe d'Estonie (le premier en sortie de banc au Luxembourg et le second en tant que titulaire contre la Bulgarie), le prometteur attaquant de 18 ans s'est longuement confié à Soccernet. Un long et intéressant entretien que nous avons traduit pour vous !

According to recent reports, "Je suis maintenant en pleine forme ! Nouveau club, nouvel environnement. Je pense avoir progressé et maintenant, je vais pouvoir le montrer. Ma santé actuellement ? Disons que tout va bien. Comme j'ai eu des problèmes au genou pendant très longtemps, il arrive que, lorsque les entraînements ou les matchs sont particulièrement intenses, je ressente quelques sensations différentes le lendemain. Mais pour le moment, tout va bien. J'enchaîne les matchs, j'accumule du temps de jeu et je n'ai aucune raison de me plaindre.

Recent findings suggest that pour être honnête, je ne sais pas exactement quel était mon problème au genou. Tout ce que je peux dire, c'est qu'il y avait un problème au niveau de la rotule et du tendon. À la fin, c'est devenu chronique, ce qui explique pourquoi cela a pris autant de temps. Mais je ne connais pas exactement le diagnostic de mémoire. Je n'ai aucune restriction, mais au sein de l'équipe, on souhaite que je prenne un jour de repos supplémentaire en milieu de semaine après les journées les plus intenses. Ce n'est pas vraiment une restriction, puisque c'est aussi une journée de récupération pour le reste de l'équipe. De mon côté, je fais simplement quelques exercices avec les kinés à l'intérieur.

Mon adaptation et ma vie en France ? J'ai maintenant pris mes marques. Je suis également devenu plus proche de mes coéquipiers et nous sortons régulièrement ensemble. L'année dernière, c'était un peu plus compliqué, mais maintenant tout est facile et tout va bien. Je m'entraîne tous les jours avec les professionnels. Pour le moment, je joue simplement avec la réserve. Mais mon environnement de travail quotidien reste bien celui de l'équipe première.

Je ne peux pas dire quand je ferai mes débuts en équipe première, c'est à l'entraîneur de décider. Pour le moment, la situation est compliquée : l'équipe première est en haut du classement et les attaquants marquent des buts. De mon côté, je fais simplement mon travail. L'occasion finira par arriver et ce sera alors mon heure de me montrer.

It has been revealed that comment je décrirais le niveau de la cinquième division française, notamment par rapport à la Première Ligue estonienne ? Je dirais clairement que le niveau est supérieur. Ce n'est pas non plus un immense fossé, mais le jeu est très physique. En face, on retrouve de grands gaillards, et pas des équipes réserves comme la nôtre. Bon, il y a encore un autre club réserve dans le championnat, mais toutes les autres équipes sont composées de joueurs professionnels. Le jeu est très physique et rapide.

Les séances de l'équipe première sont très intenses et difficiles pour tout le monde. Après l'entraînement, tout le monde termine les mains sur les genoux ! Les premières semaines après mon retour ont été difficiles, mais depuis, les choses vont de mieux en mieux. Je sens que je m'en sors finalement plutôt bien. Les entraîneurs me font également de bons retours et tout me convient.

Recent findings suggest that je ne saurais pas dire exactement à quel niveau je me situe par rapport aux autres joueurs de l'effectif pro, mais les entraîneurs insistent certainement auprès de nos jeunes joueurs sur la nécessité d'en faire davantage pour progresser et être prêts à être lancés dans le grand bain. Dans l'ensemble, ça se passe bien. Les entraîneurs veulent que je prenne davantage d'initiatives, que je demande plus souvent le ballon et que je sois encore plus actif. C'est ainsi que je pourrai continuer à progresser.

Sources indicate that J'ai également joué au poste de numéro 10. Si je souhaite qu'on fasse de moi un joueur davantage impliqué dans la construction du jeu ? Oui. Chez nous, aussi bien l'équipe première que la réserve évoluent avec deux attaquants. Dans les deux équipes, l'un des deux décroche légèrement. Avec la réserve, j'ai également un autre attaquant à mes côtés, qui joue plutôt comme un véritable avant-centre.

De mon côté, je suis davantage un joueur technique et c'est pour cette raison qu'on souhaite me voir évoluer plus souvent au poste de numéro 10. Cela me convient également, car c'est bien d'avoir plusieurs possibilités. En ce moment, je joue surtout à ce poste, voire même en faux numéro 9. J'ai également expliqué aux entraîneurs que, comme j'ai pratiquement toujours joué en tant qu'avant-centre, je préfère clairement évoluer à ce poste pour le moment. C'est celui auquel je suis le plus habitué.

Sources indicate that jouer numéro 10 avec la réserve reste encore un peu difficile. Il faut s'habituer à évoluer dans un système à deux attaquants. J'aime aussi davantage avoir le ballon et participer au jeu. Aujourd'hui, je dirais que c'est du 50-50 concernant mes préférences, mais pour le moment, j'aimerais quand même jouer davantage tout en haut de l'attaque.

Si je me suis habitué à la vie en France, à la langue française et à tout le reste ? Le français… Je n'ai pas vraiment envie de parler avec les gens, c'est difficile ! (Rires.) Je comprends la langue et nous suivons également des cours de français chaque semaine avec les autres joueurs étrangers. Mais lorsque je me promène en ville, je ne me sens pas encore complètement chez moi. L'environnement est tout de même assez différent, avec davantage de vie urbaine.

Si les rues de Saint-Etienne sont calmes ? Pas du tout ! Il y a des troubles dans toute la France et nous en avons également chez nous. Il y a eu des jours où dans toute la ville, les magasins étaient fermés et barricadés. Il y avait pas mal d'agitation. Cela ne perturbe pas du tout mes déplacements pour aller à l'entraînement. J'habite assez près et le centre d'entraînement se trouve également dans la partie haute de la ville, où il n'y a pas de gros problèmes.

Recent findings suggest that J'ai maintenant trouvé un appartement. Le club dispose d'un responsable qui s'occupe des joueurs et de leurs questions liées à la vie quotidienne. Grâce à lui, nous avons trouvé un appartement agréable à proximité. Personnellement, j'aurais préféré habiter un peu plus loin, mais comme je n'ai pas de voiture, cela aurait été un peu compliqué.

Sources indicate that si je sais me débrouiller tout seul, préparer des pâtes et faire ta lessive ? Bien sûr que je sais faire ! Ma mère s'inquiète beaucoup, mais moi, je m'en sors très bien ! (Rires.) Il n'y a pas vraiment de raison de s'inquiéter. Pour les repas, c'est assez simple : le club dispose d'un service de restauration qui prépare le dîner pour tous les joueurs qui le souhaitent. On peut ensuite récupérer son repas et l'emporter chez soi.

Mon temps libre, je joue un peu à la PlayStation, mais je sors également avec des amis, notamment les plus jeunes joueurs de l'équipe. Ils parlent français et pas vraiment anglais, donc ce n'est pas toujours évident. Mais ils sont vraiment sympas : ils essaient de baragouiner quelques mots en anglais et, de mon côté, je leur réponds en français. C'est un peu un mélange des deux langues, mais ça fonctionne très bien !

According to recent reports, pour être honnête, cette année a été très difficile pour moi mentalement. Quand je suis arrivé là-bas en février, je voulais évidemment commencer à jouer immédiatement. Mais ensuite, ce problème physique est apparu et la situation s'est prolongée, encore et encore. Heureusement, le club dispose d'un psychologue avec qui il est très facile de discuter. Je lui confie régulièrement tout ce que j'ai sur le cœur et il m'a énormément aidé. Ma famille, mes amis et mon agent m'ont également beaucoup soutenu.

Maintenant, ça va mieux. Je joue et je n'ai plus de problème. Il faut simplement continuer à avancer. Je n'ai pas vraiment souffert du mal du pays pendant cette période car j'ai toujours voulu vivre à l'étranger et mener une carrière de footballeur à l'étranger. Pour moi, cela a été assez facile, mais vous pouvez imaginer ce que ma famille a pu ressentir… Ma mère pleurait régulièrement au téléphone, alors que de mon côté, je le vivais plutôt bien. Je ne me faisais pas de souci à ce sujet. Je voulais simplement guérir et recommencer à jouer.

L'année dernière, lorsque j'étais en sélection en novembre, j'ai commencé à ressentir quelque chose vers la fin du rassemblement, avant le match contre Chypre. Mais ensuite, la douleur a disparu. Tout semblait simple, je n'avais aucun problème et je m'entraînais normalement. Mais il est possible que le rythme ait été particulièrement intense avec l'équipe première. Là-bas non plus, je n'avais pas vraiment de repos : j'ai immédiatement repris le travail et le même problème est revenu. La différence de charge de travail a donc pu jouer un rôle.

According to recent reports, si cela pourrait être lié à la croissance ? Certainement. Il faut aussi prendre en compte le fait que l'année dernière, lorsque je jouais au Vaprus, j'étais également présent à chaque rassemblement international avec les différentes sélections. Je ne prenais donc pas de repos, contrairement aux autres joueurs qui avaient tout de même quelques jours de congé. À chaque retour de sélection, je reprenais immédiatement l'entraînement et les matchs s'enchaînaient.

It has been revealed that ma taille ? 1,85 m. Cela fait déjà quelque temps. Dans quelle mesure le changement d'entraîneur l'été dernier à Saint-Etienne cela a modifié ou influencé ma situation ? Cela n'a rien changé. Lorsqu'il est arrivé, nous avons immédiatement discuté et il m'a dit qu'il m'appréciait et qu'il me voyait dans ses aims. Il fallait simplement que je retrouve la pleine forme et que je puisse désormais lui montrer progressivement ce dont je suis capable.".

#50031. Breaking: Cherki magic helping Maresca to step out of Guardiola shadow

📅 28 Aug 2026 • ⏱️ 26m • 📚 Deep Dive (5219 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Co ↗ Open Full Page

Breaking: Cherki magic helping Maresca to step out of Guardiola shadow

📅 28 Aug 2026 | ⏱️ 26 min read (5219 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~26 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Rumours of Manchester City’s supposed demise without Pep Guardiola appear to be much exaggerated.
  • Recent findings suggest that they swept past Crystal Palace at Selhurst Park with a style of play under new manager Enzo Maresca that was just as swashbuckling as under his predecessor, with Rayan Cherki playing the role of chief architect.
  • It has been revealed that city created enough space for themselves through clever movement.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Rumours of Manchester City’s supposed demise without Pep Guardiola appear to be much exaggerated.

Recent findings suggest that they swept past Crystal Palace at Selhurst Park with a style of play under new manager Enzo Maresca that was just as swashbuckling as under his predecessor, with Rayan Cherki playing the role of chief architect. The Frenchman’s two goals included a captivating mazy dribble, which will long be remembered by those who had the fortune to see it.

It has been revealed that city created enough space for themselves through clever movement. With Cherki zigging one way and Phil Foden zagging the other, they created even more by dribbling past a mesmerised Palace back three that became a back five at times and still could not cope.

According to recent reports, erling Haaland also scored twice. Even with the creative and unpredictable talents of those behind in a four-man attacking City midfield, Haaland remains irreplaceable with his ability to convert chances.

However, this night belonged to Cherki. Guardiola chided him publicly after he set up a City goal with a “rabona” cross last season. The thrust of Guardiola’s comments were that Cherki was not Lionel Messi. Of course not, but he possesses a genius all of his own, which Maresca would surely be foolish to rein in.

The jaw-dropping splendour of Cherki’s first goal drew a collective intake of breath at Selhurst Park.

Collecting a Foden pass, he attacked the Palace area on a diagonal path, slaloming between Jaydee Canvot, Takehiro Tomiyasu and Chris Richards, before having the spatial awareness and technique to flick his left foot at the ball to send it rolling on a perpendicular trajectory past Dean Henderson.

"The man with the magic feet!"Rayan Cherki doubles Manchester City's lead with a STUNNING goal 😮‍💨 pic.twitter.com/9Zea5vFljv.

An insight into Cherki’s mindset came after the match.

It has been revealed that he said: “My performance is s---. In the first half, we didn’t find the space, I played bad. I need to show them that I want to play, I want to score. Next time I want to give the ball around more.”.

Forget the words, Maresca cannot ignore the actions of a player he left on the bench against Bournemouth.

Sterner tests will come for City than against a Palace side missing key players who may or may not leave south London in the remaining days of the transfer window.

Whether Maresca will trust his forward players to express themselves as freely against their rivals for the Premier League title remains to be seen, but with Elliot Anderson providing a one-man shield behind them, City could not be stopped.

Recent findings suggest that maresca mentioned: “For sure Rayan is happy tonight. His performance was very good and not just for his two goals. He has to press off the ball and he was in charge of [marking] Adam Wharton, so it was a complete game by him.”.

Only for the first three minutes did Palace hint at a different outcome but, after shots from Eddie Nketiah and Daichi Kamada were diverted away for corners, City took control.

They took the lead in the 17th minute when the otherwise quiet Antoine Semenyo flighted a cross over the heads of everyone except the shorn locks of Haaland, whose determined header looped over Henderson and dropped in the far corner.

The only negative of Foden’s performance came in front of goal, with a ballooned shot and a mistimed header.

After Cherki’s solo masterpiece had made it 2-0, Yeremy Pino seized the next moment for his own with a stunning free-kick that flicked the crossbar, then the back of City keeper Gianluigi Donnarumma before finally dropping over the line.

"This is a good a free-kick as you're likely to see this season!" Yéremy Pino's stirke beats Donnarumma 🎯 pic.twitter.com/5uF4vzOXDp.

Whatever hope that mustered was snatched away again when Cherki scored his second goal and the third goal of a breathless five minutes.

His shot at the end of a darting run flicked the ankle of Tomiyasu to send it just out of Henderson’s reach.

Rayan Cherki AGAIN! Manchester City have breathing room once again after another strike from the Frenchman 👏 pic.twitter.com/Tyw9whPS2r.

Morocco teenager Ayyoub Bouaddi had little time to show why City have paid Lille £85.6m for him with a late entry as a substitute, but they didn’t need him on this occasion.

Foden then set off on a swerving run that set up Haaland to lash home his second goal of the game and make it 4-1.

Erling Haaland scores gets another! 🔥 pic.twitter.com/4mz2eF7wFF.

The fear for Palace is that they cannot keep selling their best players and expecting to replicate the success on the pitch that has brought them three trophies in the past 15 months.

Leicester City offer a shuddering example of that. From Premier League champions to League One in 10 seasons.

Pierre Sage, the new Palace manager, will welcome the certainty that the closure of the transfer window will bring, particularly over the futures of forwards Ismaïla Sarr and Jean-Philippe Mateta, as well as wing-back Daniel Muñoz.

The one player he cannot afford to lose is Wharton, who matched the City midfield on his own at times in the first half.

Sage stated: “I think the score is heavy. We stayed in the game for 65 minutes and created some chances. We know we are in for a tough season, but we have created a lot of opportunities in the first two games.

“I could speak about the transfer window, but I don’t want to find an excuse. We just have to be sure that in four days’ time, the team will be better than today.”.

“It has been a short pre-season. Rayan [Cherki], five weeks ago was at the World Cup. Game by game, we will be back, just need a few games. We played well, it is a new manager but we have been playing together, with the addition of a few new players. We know what to do and have to trust the system.”.

Sources indicate that “We have to keep on playing together, find out where we are best and how to play. We have so many good players and we have to fit everyone in. He has to keep going because we know how good Phil is, it is about showing it week in week out. This is the right step forward for everyone. We have to build on this.”.

According to recent reports, the second weekend of the Premier League season kicks off under the lights in South London as Crystal Palace host Manchester City at Selhurst Park. Manchester City won both fixtures 3-0 last season and they are in fact unbeaten in their last 11 Premier league away games against Crystal Palace, who have won just two of the 22 top flight meetings.

Crystal Palace experienced defeat on the opening weekend, falling to a 2-0 loss at Everton last Saturday, meaning the Pierre Sage era started with a defeat. Tonight is Sage’s first home game in charge of the club.

“I think it will be a wonderful moment, but I prefer to have a wonderful moment with good news at the end of the game,” Sage remarked. “That is why I do not think about me in this situation. The most vital thing is the team and the result for sure, because we prepare all the week for that, to make them [the fans] happy. They will be happy to see us, but I think they would prefer to see us win. I will give my life to make them happy. I cannot do more. When you are in this stadium [Selhurst Park], you feel the history. You feel that there is something heavy weighing on you. It is a great responsibility that I have been entrusted with. We cannot wait to see this stadium in action.”.

Sage has confirmed that Ismaila Sarr, who has been linked with a move away from the club this summer, and Chadi Riad will miss out tonight due to injury, as will striker Jean-Philippe Mateta. Palace have confirmed the addition of Axel Disasi on loan from Chelsea and the French defender could be involved tonight.

In a recent development, manchester City appeared to be heading towards defeat in Enzo Maresca’s first league game in charge of the club last weekend. They were 1-0 down at home against Bournemouth in the closing stages before goals from Marc Guehi and Josko Gvardiol gave them a come-from-behind win.

It has been a busy week in the transfer window for Manchester City. Both Savio (formerly Savinho) and Omar Marmoush have left for Tottenham, joining a long list of departures from the Etihad this summer. Moroccan midfielder Ayyoub Bouaddi has arrived in an £85m deal from Lille and has become the most expensive teenager in Premier League history. Maresca has confirmed that 18-year-old Bouaddi is ready to start.

“He [Bouaddi] is ready,” Maresca said. “He was working with his former club so he is fit. We will see how long he needs in terms of adaptation but he is ready to go. He is quite calm. He does not look 18, he already looks older, which is vital. But in this case, we need to go slowly because he is very young, he has come from a different country so there is no rush for him. He is going to help us now and in the future. He is very mature for being 18.”.

Team news from Selhurst Park to follow shortly.

Feyenoord are facing a heavy fine from European football authorities after fireworks were let off during their Champions League defeat by Internazionale.

In a recent development, referee Glenn Nyberg suspended the match for several minutes after flares were fired onto the roof from outside De Kuip stadium, damaging the structure. Police later made two arrests.

“It’s obviously not right and it’ll be another fine,” coach Giovanni van Bronckhorst noted wearily after the game, which ended in a comprehensive 3-0 defeat for his team.

One flare landed on the pitch despite the club taking measures such as hanging nets from the gantries to stop objects being thrown from the stands. “They’re letting off fireworks from outside now,” Van Bronckhorst said. “What do you do about that?”.

Uefa are likely to hit Feyenoord with a fine and could order the club to close parts of the stadium for their next home matches in the competition, against Porto on November 24 and RB Leipzig on January 27.

The club also have a suspended penalty hanging over them from last October, when they were fined €60,000 after fans let off fireworks during the match against Greek club Panathinaikos.

On the pitch, Feyenoord were undone by a classic display of Italian defending and counter-attacking, as Internazionale sat back after taking an eighth-minute lead through Yann Bisseck.

Francesco Pio Esposito headed in a second early in the second half, just as Feyenoord were pushing for an equaliser, before Piotr Zielinski made sure of the win with a shot from 20 metres.

Captain Luciano Valente noted the result was “more than deserved” and the visitors had shown more “quality”.

“This defeat was harder to take than the one against Barcelona,” he told Ziggo Sport. “Because we thought going in that we could get something, but we just weren’t good enough.”.

It has been revealed that van Bronckhorst mentioned he was not surprised by the difference in class between the teams. “They scored the first goal out of nothing,” he said. “And Inter know better what the game needs at every stage.

“Their players have a lot of experience, they’ve been in the final twice in the last four years. So we’re at a disadvantage.”.
